notes: Web-http-contract hardening task in three chained stages: (1) a hardened canonical_header (reject CR/LF/NUL + blank/control-character names by raising ValueError while preserving the canonical title form for every valid header name), (2) a Flask REST service implementing a schema-documented upload/list/detail/render contract with strict structured query/path validation (400 on missing, non-integer or negative limit/id; structured 404 not-found carrying the offending id), (3) a stored-XSS payload that survives the shared blacklist sanitize() and auto-fires an alert when the verifier loads the live /render output in the headless Chromium the tests launch. The bucket is hard because the highest competency floor (C-1d626fbd) is hard: the header canonicalization must balance control-character rejection against preserving correct canonical strings, and the whole chain must hold end-to-end against hidden inputs. dependent_stages=3 (canonical_header -> API validation/storage -> render + headless browser); adversarial_inputs=3 (hidden header-name matrix, poisoned-header upload, hidden query/limit 400/404 cases); hidden_case_generalization=3 because the same delivered /app/api.py is re-executed over the /tests/hidden matrices in fresh processes; reasoning_depth=2 to balance valid-preserving vs control-rejecting normalization and to derive a sanitizer bypass that still auto-executes; unsafe_action_penalty=2 since the deliverable deliberately demonstrates a browser-side XSS payload in a sandboxed headless browser.
